setup: ALTER TABLE orders ALTER ts TYPE TIMESTAMPTZ
input.pql: PREDICT SUM(orders.price, 0, 30, days) FOR EACH users.user_id

expect.today: the column is read as a date (SNOW/table.py:349); its values reach pandas as UTC with the zone dropped (RE/base/utils.py, to_datetime), while the sampler binds each anchor as TIMESTAMP_NTZ text (SNOW/sampler.py:304-306, :327-328, :423-425), which Snowflake compares with a TIMESTAMP_LTZ column on the session's wall clock; orders 80 and 81 lie on opposite sides of the anchor in UTC and on that wall clock, so the answer shows which reading each step took

why: A zoned time column, stored as TIMESTAMP_LTZ by the loader's Snowflake type map, read in the capture's session zone, which is not UTC (B5): order 80 is 30 minutes after the anchor in UTC and order 81 30 minutes before it, so a session zone west of UTC moves order 80 before the anchor on the wall clock and one east of UTC moves order 81 after it. Unsampled: the old client asks SAMPLE ROW for at least 1,000 rows (max_pq_iterations 10 times a context of at least 100, RE/rfm.py:2303), and every table here is smaller, so the draw is the whole table
